# Release planning

Our business has a strong seasonality: customers are receptive in September and January, and almost deaf in August and the last two weeks of December. A release planned for the wrong window is wasted effort, so the calendar comes first and the feature list second. I mark the windows on a yearly calendar and ask for each candidate: is it ripe, and does it fit the window?

A glut of launches is as bad as an empty quarter. When three big features ripen in the same month, customers notice none of them. I spread the releases, hold back what is not quite ready and keep a few small improvements in reserve for the quiet weeks.

Revisit the plan every quarter, because the windows move.
